A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work by the same authors. All 36 pages of v1 and 41 pages of v3, including Appendices A–D, support comparison. BAG, ReBAG and ReBAG-S correspond to MoVE, ROVE and ROVEs despite the changed title and terminology.

before.justification: Section 3 and Appendix D report original optimization and model-selection experiments, including hyperparameter profiling, tail-heaviness tests and runtime comparisons.

after.justification: Section 3 and Appendix D report original stochastic-programming experiments and synthetic and real-data regression results, including mean costs, tail probabilities and confidence intervals.

M1.justification: The majority-vote and two-phase epsilon-optimality architectures remain. Algorithms 1–2 now accept a generic, possibly randomized learner instead of requiring an empirical-objective minimizer. Algorithm 2 permits separate retrieval and voting subsample sizes, k1 and k2, and evaluates candidates using sample-mean loss instead of v1's generic empirical objective. These are adaptations within the retained voting framework.

E1.justification: v3 adds synthetic regression and six UCI datasets: Wine Quality, Bike Sharing, Online News, Appliances Energy, Superconductivity and Gas Turbine Emission. It removes v1's LASSO-based model-selection task and replaces the six-asset integer CVaR portfolio problem with continuous, ten-asset mean-variance optimization. Appendix D also adds a network-design scenario with strongly correlated objectives.

E2.justification: The new regression comparisons evaluate unensembled Adam-trained MLPs, least-squares regression and ridge regression against their ensemble variants. v1 Figure 11's comparison of SAA-based ensembles against standalone Wasserstein DRO across ambiguity radii is removed. DRO remains evaluated as a base learner in v3 Figure 16, corresponding to v1 Figure 3.

E3.justification: v3 introduces MLP training/validation splits of 70%/30%, early stopping, standardized real datasets with half-training/half-testing splits, and a million-sample synthetic test set. Its continuous-problem defaults use k1=max(30,n/2), k2=max(30,n/200) and B1=50, whereas v1 used a shared k=max(10,n/200) and B1=20. Most discrete-problem defaults remain unchanged; additional protocols include loss-tail evaluation and larger-subsample network-design controls.

E4.justification: Most original subsample-size, ensemble-size, epsilon, optima-multiplicity and tail-heaviness analyses are retained or relocated. v3 adds comparisons across MLP depths and synthetic input dimensions, plus network-design controls for larger subsamples and strongly correlated objectives (Figures 1, 10–13 and 15). These substantially extend the analysis of capacity sensitivity and conditions limiting ensemble benefits.

E5.justification: v1 reports averages over more than 50 repetitions without empirical confidence intervals. v3 adds 95% confidence intervals to regression and stochastic-programming cost plots and specifies 200 independently generated synthetic datasets and 100 real-data permutations. These disclosures do not establish increased repetitions for retained experiments; their former general repetition-count statement is no longer provided.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive regression mean-cost and tail-probability results, together with results for the replacement portfolio task and additional network scenarios. Figure 2 shows markedly lighter ROVE tails on three of six real datasets, while ROVEs underperforms the base learner; Figure 10a also reports a low-capacity ROVEs failure. v1's model-selection, CVaR and standalone-DRO-sweep results are removed. Results under replacement settings do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v3 recasts Theorem 1 using the base learner's excess-risk tail E and revises Theorem 2 for separate k1/k2 and learner-risk versus sample-mean-deviation terms. The original gap-based bound survives in Appendix C's Theorem 3. Appendix C generalizes U-statistic concentration to nonsymmetric kernels and independent learner randomness, with corresponding proof changes. v1's Proposition 1 and unique-optimum corollary are removed.

C1.justification: The central scientific claim remains that model-level voting can convert polynomial excess-risk-tail decay into exponential decay for suitable base learners, with average-regret benefits in discrete spaces. v3's title and ensemble terminology clarify this already specified guarantee. The expanded experiments support the retained headline contribution.

C2.justification: v1 recommends BAG for problems with a unique optimum; v3 recommends ROVE for general use. New interpretations connect network-depth effects to expressiveness and bias, real-data ROVEs failures to data splitting, and weaker network-design benefits to correlated objectives canceling noise. The bias limitation remains, but v1's explicit concluding caveat that tail improvement need not reduce expected regret outside discrete problems is dropped.

D1.justification: v3 adds code-access links and substantial implementation documentation: MLP layer widths and activations, Adam and stopping details, preprocessing, synthetic-data generation and phase-specific configurations (Section 3 and Appendix D). These are documented access and implementation additions; the linked resources were not inspected. v1's Apple M1 Pro and 16 GB hardware disclosure is removed.

R1.justification: v3 adds a substantial ensemble-learning discussion covering subagging, boosting and stacking, with citations including Dietterich, Zhou, Wolpert and Chen–Guestrin. It explicitly positions model-level selection against prediction aggregation in existing ensembles. Much of v1's heavy-tail and learning-to-optimize review is retained and moved into Section 4, while Appendix A retains bagging for stochastic optimization.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten, with changed terminology and mathematical notation throughout. Hyperparameter profiling moves from Section 3.1 to Appendix D.3, regression leads the experimental section, related work gains a main-text section, and Appendix D is reorganized around architectures, problems, profiling and additional results.

P2.justification: v3 introduces numerous regression and tail-probability panels, adds confidence bars, restructures the main optimization figure and redraws retained plots with revised labels and axes. Profiling, light-tail and DRO-base figures move into the appendix, while the standalone-DRO comparison disappears. Typography, title/author layout and figure placement also change substantially.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens evidence for the paper's broad learning applicability: v1 chiefly evaluates optimization and discrete model selection, while v3 directly tests continuous regression, six real datasets and loss-tail behavior, with uncertainty reporting for mean costs. The randomized-learner analysis and added implementation information further improve applicability and reproducibility, while reported failures clarify practical boundaries. These gains outweigh the removed standalone-DRO comparison, unique-optimum corollary and some reproducibility and limitation details.
